correctness.rationale: Erickson–Kretschmann Proposition 5.1 gives all distinct normalized corner rectangles and row/column strips for this sign convention. There are 2(n-1)^2 corners and 2n strips, also at n=2. On their supports the entries are constant, so squared norms are 1/(ab) and 1/n. Counting gives the exact Mellin formula and strip probability n^(1-s)/[(H_(n-1)^(s))^2+n^(1-s)]. Conditionally on a corner the two orientations are equiprobable and both side lengths have the independent truncated weights a^(-s). Integral comparison for partial sums proves the Beta and log-uniform limits; above s=1 the omitted zeta tail is exactly the one-coordinate total variation error. In the moving window, a partial sum to min(n-1,floor(n^t)) equals log(n) times the integral of exp(-lambda*u) on [0,t], up to bounded error, by monotone sum/integral comparison. The strip numerator is exp(-lambda), negligible compared with log(n)^2. Independence yields the joint limit. In the untilted case the inverse product of the two rescaled lengths converges in distribution to 1/(UV) because the axes are limit-null; strip probability tends to zero even though the strip variable itself is large. Integration over UV<1/z gives (1+log z)/z. Substitution of the three harmonic-sum orders into the exact formula yields all moment constants; the strip term is negligible in each. Collision conditioning is with respect to the initially uniform distinct vertex law.
